title: Claiming Service: Harriet Tubman and the Pension Fight
setting: Washington, D.C., 1898-1899. Auburn, New York, remains offstage because the provided source pages do not describe playable scenes there.
description: A source-grounded investigation game about Harriet Tubman’s Civil War pension claim. The player works through a congressional file, compares what the papers say about her service, and decides what kind of recognition to recommend.
learningObjectives: Describe the Civil War services Harriet Tubman performed for the Union.
Explain how Congress handled Tubman’s pension claim and on what basis it was finally granted.
Evaluate whether Congress officially acknowledged Tubman’s own wartime service.

player.name: Committee Clerk
player.brief: You sort papers, question visitors, and draft recommendations on Harriet Tubman’s pension claim.

sharedContext.text: You are a clerk sorting Harriet Tubman’s pension papers. The file says House records were used to examine her Civil War service, including work as a nurse, cook, and spy. Yet the summary also says she later received a pension only as a veteran’s widow. Your job is to trace what the papers claim, how Congress handled them, and what that final choice did not officially recognize.

endings.title: File Closed Too Soon
endings.summary: You stop the claim before it reaches its later bill-and-report stage. In your version of events, the office treats the case as unfinished and lets the chance for formal recognition shrink away.

historicalOutcome.text: The provided pages show that the claim did continue into 1899 through later records, and the summary says Tubman ultimately secured a pension only as a widow of a Civil War veteran, not on the basis of her own service.
